h: Cotton Town and the Moors Above It
p: Blackburn was once one of the great cotton-weaving towns of Lancashire, and the Victorian mills and terraces still give the place its character. It even made its way into pop history: the line about four thousand holes in Blackburn, Lancashire, in the Beatles' A Day in the Life came from a newspaper story about the state of the town's roads. A fun bit of trivia for the drive in.

Blackburn Museum and Art Gallery, in the town centre, is a good free stop for families, with local history and some surprising collections. Queen's Park, on the eastern side of town, is a traditional Victorian park with a lake and plenty of space for a wander.

If the weather's kind, head for the hills. Darwen Tower stands proudly on the moors above neighbouring Darwen, and the walk up rewards you with sweeping views across Lancashire on a clear day. It's a bit of a climb, so save it for kids with sturdy legs, or tackle it before the bouncing.

West of town, Hoghton Tower is a striking hilltop house with a long history, open on selected days, and the Ribble Valley is just to the north, with Clitheroe and its castle making an easy and pretty drive.
Back at the Soccordome, the building is also home to football pitches, so evenings and weekends can be busy with teams coming and going. Leave a bit of time for parking.
Put it all together and Blackburn has more going for it than you might think, especially if you mix a high-energy session with some proper Lancashire scenery.
